title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
shortDescription: Build essential knowledge across systems, networks and modern threats.
description: A practical starting point for understanding how systems work, where risk appears and how security teams protect what matters.
alt: Cybersecurity Fundamentals course at Cyberus Academy
outcome: Build a dependable foundation for every security pathway.
audience: People beginning a cybersecurity career or building a reliable technical foundation.
assessment: Weekly lab checkpoints, scenario reviews and a final defensive walkthrough.

faqs.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. It starts with the language and concepts needed to build a dependable security foundation.

faqs.question: How much weekly time should I plan?
faqs.answer: Plan for two live learning sessions plus three to five hours of guided practice each week.

title: Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing
shortDescription: Learn to find weaknesses, validate risk and communicate findings responsibly.
description: Practice the disciplined attacker mindset used to discover, validate and report security weaknesses in authorized environments.
alt: Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing course at Cyberus Academy
outcome: Practice reconnaissance, validation and responsible reporting.
audience: Learners with basic networking knowledge who want to practice offensive security responsibly.
assessment: Reconnaissance exercises, controlled validation tasks and a professional penetration-test report.

faqs.question: Is exploitation performed against real systems?
faqs.answer: No. All exercises run in authorized Cyberus sandbox environments.

faqs.question: Do I need a security background?
faqs.answer: Networking fundamentals are recommended, but the course builds the testing workflow step by step.

title: Security Operations (SOC)
shortDescription: Investigate alerts, understand telemetry and respond with clarity.
description: Build the investigation habits required to triage alerts, correlate evidence and make clear response decisions in a SOC environment.
alt: Security Operations SOC course at Cyberus Academy
outcome: Turn noisy signals into confident security decisions.
format: Live classes and simulated SOC lab
audience: Aspiring SOC analysts and defenders who want structured practice with security telemetry.
assessment: Alert triage drills, investigation write-ups and a final simulated incident response.

faqs.question: Will I work with realistic alerts?
faqs.answer: Yes. The labs use simulated telemetry and investigation scenarios modeled on SOC workflows.

faqs.question: Is this useful for a first SOC role?
faqs.answer: It is designed to build the practical investigation habits expected in entry-level analyst work.

title: Cloud Security
shortDescription: Secure cloud environments with practical controls and useful visibility.
description: Learn how identity, configuration, workloads and monitoring combine to create resilient cloud security outcomes.
alt: Cloud Security course at Cyberus Academy
outcome: Design stronger visibility and control across cloud workloads.
audience: Security and technology professionals moving into cloud-focused roles.
prerequisites: Familiarity with one cloud platform is helpful
assessment: Configuration reviews, identity design exercises and a final cloud security architecture brief.

faqs.question: Do I need an active cloud account?
faqs.answer: No. Guided labs provide the environments needed for the course exercises.

faqs.question: Can I focus on one cloud provider?
faqs.answer: The principles transfer across providers, with examples that compare common cloud patterns.

title: Digital Forensics
shortDescription: Preserve evidence, trace activity and turn signals into a defensible story.
description: Develop a careful, evidence-led approach to collecting, examining and explaining digital activity during an investigation.
alt: Digital Forensics course at Cyberus Academy
outcome: Build an evidence-led approach to investigation.
audience: Analysts and investigators who want a structured foundation in digital forensics.
assessment: Artifact examination exercises, timeline reconstruction and a final forensic findings report.

faqs.question: Are the evidence sets safe to use?
faqs.answer: Yes. All evidence is curated for training and handled inside the lab environment.

faqs.question: Is this an incident response course?
faqs.answer: It provides a strong forensic foundation that complements incident response work.

title: Governance, Risk & Compliance
shortDescription: Connect technical security work to policy, risk and resilient outcomes.
description: Understand how security programs turn business context, risk decisions and controls into accountable action.
alt: Governance Risk and Compliance course at Cyberus Academy
outcome: Translate security priorities into accountable action.
audience: Security, audit and technology professionals connecting controls to business risk.
prerequisites: Ability to read basic business processes
assessment: Risk assessment workshop, control mapping exercise and a final executive security brief.

faqs.question: Is this course only for compliance teams?
faqs.answer: No. It is useful for anyone who needs to connect security decisions to organizational risk.

faqs.question: Which framework does the course follow?
faqs.answer: The exercises use transferable control and risk concepts with references to common frameworks.
